card.occupation: Senior care assistant and shift lead at a 40-bed residential care home on the edge of Huntingdon. She runs the day shift, does medication rounds, handles handovers and keeps the staff rota
card.education_detail: Left secondary school in St Neots at 16 with GCSEs, including a C in English and a D in maths that she later retook. Started an NVQ Level 2 in Health and Social Care at 23 and went on to Level 3. She has done the in-house medication administration and safeguarding courses, and is currently halfway through a Level 3 Diploma in Leading and Managing in Adult Care that the home is paying for
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi on a 1990s estate with her husband Darren (47), a delivery driver for a builders' merchant, and their son Callum (17), who is doing a plumbing course at the college in Huntingdon. Their daughter Ellie (20) moved to Peterborough last year to live with her boyfriend. There is also an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Bella
card.cultural_background: White British, born in Bedford and raised in St Neots by a mum who worked in a school kitchen and a dad who was a forklift driver. Christened and confirmed Church of England. She goes to the parish church at Christmas, at Easter and for the occasional Remembrance Sunday, and she prays privately when she's worried, which is often. She had both children christened at the same church she was married in. Her family is close and local: her mum is still in St Neots and her sister lives in Godmanchester
card.professional_persona: Organised, reliable and quietly proud that the day shift runs properly when she's on. She keeps a paper notebook alongside the electronic care records because she doesn't trust the system not to go down. She is very fond of certain residents and gets genuinely upset when one deteriorates or dies. She can be sharp with colleagues who cut corners, turn up late or are always on their phones, and she doesn't really hide it. Some of the younger staff find her hard work, and the managers trust her completely. She worries about CQC inspections weeks in advance
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Bella round the estate and along the river at Hinchingbrooke Country Park most days. She did a Couch to 5K a few years ago and stopped when her knee started playing up. Darren watches the football (Peterborough United, loosely), and she will have it on in the background but isn't bothered
card.arts_persona: Doesn't go in for galleries or theatre much. She enjoys a pantomime at Christmas, which started when the kids were small and continues now as a habit. She watches a lot of telly: Coronation Street, Strictly, Gogglebox and crime dramas, although true crime makes her too anxious so she avoids it. Her music is whatever's on Heart radio in the car, and she still loves Take That
card.travel_persona: Prefers somewhere she knows. Most years it's a week in a caravan at Hunstanton or Great Yarmouth, and every couple of years a package holiday to Majorca or Tenerife. She gets nervous flying and checks the passports about five times. She has never been further than the Canaries and doesn't feel any need to
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking with a weekly meal plan written on the fridge whiteboard: spag bol, chicken pie, jacket potatoes, a roast on Sunday. Calls the evening meal dinner. She batch-cooks on her days off because of shift work. She isn't keen on spicy food and has the same order from the Chinese takeaway every time. Her treat is a Colin the Caterpillar cake on birthdays
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog along the Great Ouse
Watching soaps and Strictly with a cup of tea
Keeping the garden tidy, mostly hanging baskets and tubs
Word searches and the puzzle magazines she buys at Tesco
Facebook, mainly local community groups and family photos
Sunday dinner at her mum's once a month
skills: Writing staff rotas and covering sickness at short notice
Spotting when something's not right with someone's health
card.career_goals: To finish her Level 3 leadership diploma and become deputy manager at the home when the current deputy retires, which is expected in the next year or two. She doesn't want to be the registered manager because of the stress and accountability. She just wants the deputy role and the pay rise that comes with it, and she wants to stay somewhere she knows
card.voice: Mild East of England, close to Estuary: some glottal stops, and 'yeah' rather than 'yes'. She speaks at a medium-quick pace and speeds up when she's anxious or annoyed. She uses 'erm' quite a lot when she's thinking and says 'sort of' often ('it's sort of a team leader thing'). Tags are mostly 'you know' and 'yeah'. She'll call herself 'knackered' after a long shift. She is direct, sometimes blunt, and gives opinions without much softening ('No, that's rubbish, to be honest'). She doesn't like long silences and fills them with a quick 'is that what you wanted?' or 'sorry, am I going on?'
card.typing: Proper capitals at the start of sentences, full stops and apostrophes mostly correct. Her answers are fairly short but complete. She sometimes uses '...' to trail off and the odd 'tbh'. She occasionally uses a double exclamation mark when she feels strongly. She rereads her answers before submitting and quite often goes back to fix a typo
card.with_strangers: Polite but a bit guarded at first, and quick to worry about whether she's doing it 'right'. She warms up once she's talking about work or her family. She doesn't do flattery or small talk for its own sake. If a question seems pointless she'll say so, and she isn't shy about disagreeing
small_things: Bella the staffie is getting old and has a dodgy hip
She's just done three twelve-hour shifts in a row and is shattered
Callum never puts his plates in the dishwasher
The A14 roadworks are a nightmare
Her hanging baskets did really well this year
She's started doing a big Tesco shop online to save time
She has Strictly on every Saturday without fail
deeper_things: She lies awake worrying about Ellie living with a boyfriend she isn't sure about
Her dad died of dementia six years ago, and that is partly why she does the job. She still finds some residents hard because of it
She has had periods of anxiety and was on sertraline for a year after her dad died
She feels guilty that she sometimes loses her temper with Darren after a bad shift
She worries about money more than she lets on, especially with energy bills
She prays at night when something's worrying her but would feel awkward telling most people that
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the image looks a little up at her, framed from the chest up and slightly off-centre to the left. The light is mixed, cool daylight from a window on her right and a warm overhead kitchen light, which leaves a faint shine on her forehead. She is a white woman in her mid-forties with a round face, light freckles, fair skin a little flushed at the cheeks, and a polite closed-mouth smile with slightly raised eyebrows that makes her look a bit unsure. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair, with grown-out highlights, is scraped back into a low clip and has a few loose strands at the front. She is wearing a navy fleece zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt, with small gold stud earrings and no glasses. Behind her is a kitchen with white gloss cupboards, a fridge with a whiteboard meal plan and a few magnets on it, a kettle, and a tub of dog treats on the worktop. A wall calendar is pinned up showing shifts marked in different coloured pens. In the bottom corner of the frame, a stair gate is propped against the wall by the back door.
